title: Reorganize build targets, add QuickCI lightweight runner, and per-file linting
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Introduces QuickCI (opt-in lightweight CI), per-file linting to reduce job runtime, and splits monolithic build targets into smaller, cache-friendly units. No runtime behavior changes.
description:
Summary: This PR refactors the CI build graph and introduces an opt-in lightweight runner (QuickCI) plus a per-file linting mode to dramatically reduce CI latency for small changes. It also reorganizes build targets into smaller, cache-friendly units and pins a small set of GH Actions to SHAs for reproducibility. Motivation: Our full CI run averages ~22m for small README/typo PRs. This work targets fast feedback for iterative developer work while preserving full CI coverage for merge commits. Changes are gated behind an opt-in flag (QUICK_CI=true) so teams can adopt incrementally.

What I changed (high level):
- Add .github/workflows/quickci.yml: a lightweight pipeline that runs fast-path jobs (per-file lint, unit smoke subset, quick-typecheck).
- Update .github/workflows/ci.yml: split the large build target into smaller jobs (core-lib, serving-runtime, sdk-python, sdk-ts, docs), and add explicit cache-keying per-target.
- Implement per-file linting utility scripts/tools/perfile_lint.sh that detect changed paths (git diff --name-only) and invoke ESLint/ruff/clang-format only for impacted packages.
- Pin critical actions (actions/checkout, actions/cache, setup-python) to SHAs and add short pointer to lockfile in .github/actions-pins.md.
- Bump eslint -> 8.40.0 and pytest -> 7.4.1; update pre-commit hooks accordingly.
- Small edits to Makefile and BUILD_* entries to support targeted builds (make build-TARGET).
- Add docs: docs/dev/ci-quickci.md describing opt-in, expected latency, and how to override.

Commits (high-level):
- feat(ci): add quickci workflow and per-file linting script
- refactor(ci): split build matrix into labeled targets and per-target caches
- chore(ci): pin actions to SHAs and add actions-pins.md
- chore(deps): bump eslint, pytest, pre-commit hooks
- docs: add quickci opt-in guide and upgrade notes

Files changed (high level):
- .github/workflows/quickci.yml (new)
- .github/workflows/ci.yml (modified)
- .github/actions-pins.md (new)
- tools/perfile_lint.sh (new)
- scripts/ci_util.sh (modified)
- BUILD_TARGETS/ (new small target descriptors, 4 files)
- package.json / pyproject.toml (deps bumped)
- docs/dev/ci-quickci.md (new)
- Makefile (small changes)

Testing & CI:
- Initial CI run (first push) failed the full lint job due to a stricter ESLint rule in 8.40.0 catching a few legacy patterns in examples/; those were fixed in the follow-up commit by adding overrides for examples/* and a small code cleanup.
- After fixes, QuickCI run median latency on a sample of 50 small PRs dropped from ~22m to ~3m (per-file lint + smoke tests). Full CI runs remain unchanged in coverage; full CI median is ~28m but now split into parallelized smaller jobs which improved tail latency by ~12%.
- Cache hit rates improved by changing keys to include target-version and git-shas of deps; observed ~46% faster restore on average.

Review thread (condensed):
- Luca: "Nice ergonomics. Two asks: document opt-in and add telemetry for QuickCI adoption (percent of PRs using QUICK_CI)."
- Priya: "Added docs and a simple telemetry event in scripts/ci_telemetry.sh that emits to internal metrics when QUICK_CI=true; added note in docs/dev/ci-quickci.md."
- Rachel: "We should ensure pinning action SHAs is resurfaced in release notes and a maintenance checklist."
- Priya: "Added .github/actions-pins.md and a short section in docs/dev/ci-quickci.md about how/when to update pins; flagged ENG-2099 for rotation cadence."
- Samir: "Per-file linting looks good. Please ensure that test-only changes (tests/) still run unit tests. Also add an explicit fallback to full lint when detection fails."
- Priya: "Added detection fallback and forced full-lint for changes that touch the top-level CI configs or BUILD_TARGETS/ directory."
- Review approvals: Luca (approve), Rachel (approve after docs update), Samir (approve).

Notable implementation details and caveats:
- QuickCI is opt-in via the QUICK_CI pipeline dispatch or by setting QUICK_CI=true in a branch. The workflow is intentionally conservative: it will run only per-file lint + a small smoke test matrix. A lightweight feature flag in scripts/ci_util.sh will force full CI for branches matching release/* or when BUILD_TARGETS/ or .github/ files are modified.
- Per-file linting uses a path->tool map in tools/perfile_lint.sh. We keep a short whitelist of directories where per-file linting is safe; touching other directories triggers full-lint.
- Action SHAs pinned for reproducibility; see .github/actions-pins.md for the list and rationale. Pin maintenance will be tracked under ENG-2099.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge this PR to main behind an env toggle (QUICK_CI opt-in).
2) Infra/Platform teams can enable QUICK_CI for high-frequency test repos and pilot teams.
3) After 2 weeks of telemetry and any follow-ups, enable as default for PRs that are small (<= 10 files changed) and do not touch CI configs.

Follow-ups (tracked in Linear/JIRA):
- ENG-1245: Add telemetry dashboards and adoption metrics for QuickCI.
- ENG-2099: Quarterly rotation plan for pinned GH Action SHAs.
- SUP-8921: Support request to enable QuickCI for some customer-facing repos; included as linked_jira.

Merge notes: Squash-and-merge. After merge, I ran a smoke of 10 internal PRs to validate the probability of false negatives in per-file lint detection; none of the smoke PRs missed necessary checks but we left the fallback to full-lint as a safety net.

Why this is different than prior CI refactors: Earlier PRs focused on matrix pruning and cache key standardization. This change prioritizes developer feedback time (fast-path) with a conservative, auditable opt-in approach. It also introduces a minimal maintenance burden (pins + small scripts) and clear docs for teams to adopt.

If you want to test locally: see docs/dev/ci-quickci.md for the workflow dispatch steps and quick debug commands (tools/perfile_lint.sh --dry-run).

Acknowledgements: Thanks to the infra team (Luca), SDK owners (Rachel, Samir), and SRE for helping validate cache changes and test sharding.
